Beyond Logits: Coherent Hallucination Mitigation via
Attention Contrastive Decoding

Yujia Chen Affiliation: School of Information Science and Technology / National Key Laboratory of Deep Space Exploration, University of Science and Technology of China, China    Rui Sun Affiliation: Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University, China    Huayu Mai Affiliation: School of Information Science and Technology / National Key Laboratory of Deep Space Exploration, University of Science and Technology of China, China    Wangkai Li Affiliation: School of Information Science and Technology / National Key Laboratory of Deep Space Exploration, University of Science and Technology of China, China    Zhangyu He Affiliation: School of Information Science and Technology / National Key Laboratory of Deep Space Exploration, University of Science and Technology of China, China    Bingzhou Wang Affiliation: School of Information Science and Technology / National Key Laboratory of Deep Space Exploration, University of Science and Technology of China, China    Aibing Li Affiliation: School of Information Science and Technology / National Key Laboratory of Deep Space Exploration, University of Science and Technology of China, China    Wenzhang SUN Affiliation: School of Software, Tsinghua University, China    Tianzhu Zhang Affiliation: School of Information Science and Technology / National Key Laboratory of Deep Space Exploration, University of Science and Technology of China, China Correspondence to: tzzhang@ustc.edu.cn
Abstract

Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate impressive multimodal capabilities, yet suffer from hallucination—generating factually inaccurate content. Contrastive Decoding (CD) mitigates this by contrasting amateur and expert branches at the logit level. However, our investigation reveals that such logit-level interventions fundamentally compromise generation coherence, necessitating restrictive penalty constraints unrelated to hallucination suppression. We introduce Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD), a training-free plug-in that complements logit-level CD by relocating part of the contrastive operations to the attention mechanism. Operating at an earlier stage of the forward pass, ACD performs smooth semantic-preserving interventions through an Adaptive Subtraction Strategy (ASS), which attenuates hallucination-associated attention patterns while amplifying critical visual information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that combining ACD with existing CD methods (e.g., VCD+ACD) produces substantially more coherent outputs with further reduced hallucinations, eliminating restrictive penalties while enabling trustworthy multimodal generation.Code is available in https://github.com/jj-ccc/ACD.

Keywords: 
Machine Learning, ICML

1 Introduction

Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) (Liu et al., 2023b; Liu et al., 2023c; Liu et al., 2024a; Zhu et al., 2023; Bai et al., 2023; Li et al., 2023a; Driess et al., 2023; Achiam et al., 2023; Chowdhery et al., 2023; Alayrac et al., 2022) have emerged as a transformative paradigm in multimodal AI. By integrating visual encoders with large language models, LVLMs enable sophisticated cross-modal reasoning across diverse tasks, including image captioning (Lin et al., 2014; Li et al., 2023a), visual question answering (Liu et al., 2023c; Liu et al., 2023b; Liu et al., 2024a; Hudson and Manning, 2019), and complex multimodal reasoning (Lu et al., 2022; Alayrac et al., 2022; Achiam et al., 2023). This advancement establishes a foundation for more natural and intuitive human-machine interaction.

Despite significant advances in LVLMs, the “hallucination” phenomenon remains a critical challenge (Li et al., 2023c; Fu et al., 2023b; Yue et al., 2024). These hallucinations manifest as grammatically coherent outputs with factual inconsistencies relative to visual input. Unlike text-only LLM hallucinations, LVLM hallucinations exhibit distinct cross-modal characteristics, manifesting in three patterns: (1) Modal dissociation: generation detached from visual input; (2) Perceptual fabrication: hallucination of non-existent attributes (e.g., colors, quantities, spatial relations); (3) Semantic distortion: inaccurate visual content summarization. These cross-modal inconsistencies substantially undermine model credibility and pose significant safety risks in critical domains such as medical diagnostics and autonomous driving.

Alleviating hallucinations in LVLMs has emerged as a critical research focus, with training-free Contrastive Decoding (CD) strategies (Li et al., 2025; Huo et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2024c; An et al., 2025; Leng et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024c; Chen et al., 2024b) representing a prominent paradigm owing to their efficiency, flexibility, and strong interpretability. These approaches mitigate hallucinations through two principal mechanisms: hallucination induction and probability recalibration. For hallucination induction, existing methods can be categorized into three primary classes: (1) Visual Contrastive Decoding (VCD) (Leng et al., 2024) amplifies the model’s reliance on linguistic priors by introducing Gaussian noise into visual inputs or completely eliminating visual signals (Liu et al., 2024c), thereby constructing a hallucination-rich probability distribution. (2) Instructional Contrastive Decoding (ICD) (Wang et al., 2024c) employs adversarial prompts (e.g., “you are a confused object detector”) to elicit hallucinated outputs. (3) Self-Introspective Decoding (SID) (Huo et al., 2024) strategically masks high-attention visual regions during decoding to provoke hallucination generation. The probability recalibration mechanism then subtracts this artificially constructed hallucination distribution from the original generation probability. As illustrated in Figure 1(a), this approach effectively suppresses factually inconsistent content while enhancing the model’s fidelity to visual evidence, offering a convenient and theoretically interpretable solution for hallucination mitigation in LVLMs.

Despite substantial empirical evidence (Leng et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024c; Huo et al., 2024) demonstrating the efficacy of contrastive decoding (CD) strategies in mitigating LVLM hallucinations, our investigation reveals that CD approaches significantly compromise generation coherence—manifested as invalid token outputs, abrupt semantic transitions, and structural degradation—under specific operational conditions. The fundamental limitation stems from CD’s crude direct subtraction operation at the logits layer, which lacks nuanced regulation of the natural language generation process. Mathematically, this operation is equivalent to re-weighting the probability space via division, i.e., Pfinal∝Poriginal/PdistortedαP_{\text{final}}\propto P_{\text{original}}/P_{\text{distorted}}^{\alpha}. While theoretically sound for suppressing hallucinations, such aggressive penalization induces a critical side effect known as the “false positive” problem (Li et al., 2023b). Since the distorted model (negative view) retains its fundamental language modeling capabilities, it legitimately assigns high probabilities to high-frequency functional tokens (e.g., “the”, “of”). Consequently, direct logit subtraction indiscriminately penalizes these syntactically essential tokens, causing the decoding trajectory to deviate from the natural language manifold (Liu et al., 2021).

Furthermore, due to the inherent discontinuity and volatility of logits distributions, logit-level subtraction forcibly distorts vocabulary distribution probabilities, thereby disrupting the model’s intrinsic language generation mechanisms. This direct intervention inadequately accounts for contextual dependencies and logical coherence, resulting in semantic fragmentation and structural collapse in generated outputs, as visualized in Figure 1(b). Notably, since ICD and SID also operate through logit-level subtraction, they inevitably encounter identical limitations. Our systematic experiments with LLaVA-1.5-7B (Liu et al., 2023b) on the CHAIR benchmark (Yue et al., 2024) corroborate these observations: VCD consistently underperforms across multiple evaluation metrics, including CIDEr (description quality), METEOR (semantic comprehension), ROUGE-L (information completeness), and BLEU (generation precision). Additionally, GPT-5-assisted evaluation scores significantly trail those of conventional decoding methods. These empirical findings explicitly expose an inherent contradiction within current contrastive decoding paradigms—while logit-level contrastive operations effectively suppress hallucinations, they inevitably degrade linguistic quality, presenting a critical trade-off challenge for practical LVLM deployment.

Concurrently, probability recalibration mechanisms at the logits level frequently amplify tail token probabilities due to distribution discontinuities, resulting in invalid token generations. To mitigate this issue, existing contrastive decoding strategies typically incorporate adaptive penalty mechanisms to filter low-probability tokens. However, our in-depth analysis reveals that such compensatory mechanisms not only fail to adequately resolve the underlying issue but also introduce additional challenges. First, penalty mechanisms that mask low-probability tokens sacrifice decoding diversity (constraining the model to high-probability tokens exclusively). This implies that penalty mechanisms function primarily to counteract CD’s adverse effects rather than addressing the hallucination problem directly. This compensatory processing significantly restricts the richness and creativity of generated content, biasing outputs toward high-frequency, conventional expressions lacking natural linguistic variation and innovation. Second, the intensity calibration of current penalty mechanisms predominantly relies on heuristic algorithms (utilizing manually defined thresholds), severely limiting their adaptability and inevitably resulting in invalid token outputs. In diverse linguistic contexts and tasks, fixed penalty strategies inadequately accommodate variable generation requirements and cannot dynamically adjust filtering intensity based on contextual semantics, further exacerbating the inconsistency and instability of generated outputs.

To fundamentally address these limitations prevalent in existing CD methods, we propose Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD), which relocates contrastive operations from the discrete logit space to the continuous attention layer. This architectural choice leverages the attention mechanism’s inherent capacity to weight input information and adapt to contextual cues, facilitating smooth information flow (Vaswani et al., 2017; Castin et al., 2023). Consequently, ACD naturally generates more coherent outputs while circumventing the need for penalty terms and preserving generation diversity (Detailed theoretical and empirical analyses are provided in the Appendix B and C). This adaptive contrastive mechanism at the attention level not only precisely localizes and suppresses hallucination sources but also preserves the model’s intrinsic language generation capabilities, offering a more elegant and effective solution for hallucination mitigation in LVLMs. Beyond architectural relocation, ACD introduces an Adaptive Subtraction Strategy (ASS) for finer-grained hallucination control. Unlike uniform subtraction in traditional CD, ASS distinguishes between two fundamentally different attention shift patterns under hallucination induction:(1) information degradation, where decreased attention signals loss of focus on semantically relevant content that should be preserved, and (2) hallucination risk, where increased attention indicates over-focus on spurious regions that warrant suppression. Based on this assessment, ASS adaptively modulates the model’s attention allocation across different regions. Specifically, it amplifies attention to areas exhibiting information degradation while suppressing regions with hallucination risk, thereby inhibiting hallucination generation at its source and enhancing focus on semantically valid content. This fine-grained control mechanism enables the model to maintain linguistic quality while improving effective information utilization.

In summary, our main contributions are three-fold: (1) We reveal that logit-level subtraction in CD fundamentally compromises generation quality, and that penalty mechanisms fail to resolve invalid token generation while restricting output diversity. (2) We propose Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD), which relocates contrastive operations to the attention layer, leveraging attention’s inherent continuity to preserve coherence without penalties. We further introduce the Adaptive Subtraction Strategy (ASS), which distinguishes information degradation from hallucination risk to achieve precise, selective suppression. (3)Extensive experiments demonstrates ACD’s capacity to generate more coherent, higher-quality content with significantly reduced hallucinations without penalty mechanisms, advancing the SOTA in reliable LVLMs decoding.

2 Related Work

2.1 Hallucination in LVLMs

Research addressing hallucinations in large vision-language models (LVLMs) can be categorized into three primary approaches. First, contrastive decoding techniques identify and suppress hallucinated content without parameter updates. Representative methods include VCD (Leng et al., 2024), ICD (Wang et al., 2024c), and SID (Huo et al., 2024), with advanced variants such as HALC (Chen et al., 2024b), VaLiD (Wang et al., 2024b), CMVED (Li et al., 2025), PAI (Liu et al., 2024c), and AGLA (An et al., 2025) further refining these techniques through targeted attention manipulation. Second, fine-tuning strategies employ curated datasets incorporating negative (Liu et al., 2023a), counterfactual (Yu et al., 2024), or purified data (Wang et al., 2024c). Related frameworks include HALVA (Sarkar et al., 2024), HACL (Jiang et al., 2024a), PerturboLLaVA (Chen et al., 2025a), PATCH (Shang et al., 2024), HIO (Lyu et al., 2024), Octopus (Suo et al., 2025), OPA (Yang et al., 2025b), TL-DPO (Yoon et al., 2025), and VASparse (Zhuang et al., 2025). Third, direct intervention methods manipulate visual features or attention mechanisms. These include DeCo (Wang et al., 2024a), VTI (Liu et al., 2024b), VDGD (Ghosh et al., 2024), ProjectAway (Jiang et al., 2024b), TAME (Tang et al., 2025a), OPERA (Huang et al., 2024), VAR (Jiang et al., 2025b), FarSight (Tang et al., 2025b), Nullu (Yang et al., 2025a), and ClearSight (Yin et al., 2025). Notably, our method migrates contrastive decoding from logit level to attention layer, leveraging internal consistency for self-calibration rather than directly intervening in attention mechanisms.

2.2 Contrastive Decoding in Hallucination

Contrastive Decoding (CD) methods provide an elegant, training-free approach to mitigating hallucinations in LVLMs without parameter optimization. These strategies reduce hallucination generation by contrastively adjusting token probability distributions through two key mechanisms: hallucination induction and probability adjustment. Representative works include VCD (Leng et al., 2024), which injects Gaussian noise into visual inputs to construct hallucination-rich distributions; ICD (Wang et al., 2024c), which employs negative prompts to induce hallucinations; and SID (Huo et al., 2024), which strategically masks high-attention regions to expose model vulnerabilities. Advanced variants include HALC (Chen et al., 2024b) with automatic hallucination correction, VaLiD (Wang et al., 2024b) comparing early-layer outputs, CMVED (Li et al., 2025) masking cross-modal attention, PAI (Liu et al., 2024c) removing visual components entirely, and AGLA (An et al., 2025) emphasizing critical regions through image-text matching models. Several recent works also leverage attention mechanisms for hallucination mitigation, yet differ fundamentally from ACD. FarSight (Tang et al., 2025b) and DAMRO (Gong et al., 2024) modify attention within a single forward pass or use attention to select distorted tokens, but perform contrastive subtraction at the logit level. HICD (Jiang et al., 2025a) disperses attention to improve hallucination induction, again feeding results into logit-level subtraction. MoD (Chen et al., 2025c) adaptively switches between addition and subtraction but operates entirely on logits. In contrast, ACD is the first to relocate the contrastive subtraction itself from the logit space to the attention layer, eliminating the coherence degradation and penalty mechanisms inherent in all logit-level approaches. Despite demonstrated efficacy in hallucination mitigation, conventional CD strategies operate exclusively at the logits distribution level, substantially compromising output coherence and diminishing generative diversity.

3 Method

3.1 Preliminary

Vanilla Decoding. A standard LVLM θ\theta comprises a vision encoder, a vision-text interface, and an LLM decoder. Given an image vv and text query xx, the model autoregressively generates output yy via:

yt∼pθ​(yt|v,x,y<t)∝exp⁡(logitθ⁡(yt|v,x,y<t)),y_{t}\sim p_{\theta}(y_{t}|v,x,y_{<t})\propto\exp\!\left(\operatorname{logit}_{\theta}(y_{t}|v,x,y_{<t})\right), (1)

where yty_{t} is the tt-th generated token, y<ty_{<t} denotes all preceding tokens, and logitθ\operatorname{logit}_{\theta} returns the pre-softmax scores. The attention weight matrix within each decoder head is:

A=Softmax⁡(Q​K⊤d),A=\operatorname{Softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^{\top}}{\sqrt{d}}\right), (2)

where Q,K∈ℝL×dQ,K\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d} are the query and key matrices, LL is the sequence length, and dd is the head dimension. The output is then A​VAV with value matrix V∈ℝL×dV\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d}.

During autoregressive inference, the model caches KK and VV from all previous steps. The attention at step tt reduces to:

at=Softmax⁡(qt​K≤t⊤d),a_{t}=\operatorname{Softmax}\!\left(\frac{q_{t}K_{\leq t}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d}}\right), (3)

where qt∈ℝ1×dq_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times d} is the current query and K≤tK_{\leq t} aggregates cached keys. This cached attention computation serves as the intervention point for our proposed ACD.

Contrastive Decoding. CD (Leng et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024c; Huo et al., 2024) mitigates hallucinations by subtracting a hallucination-rich distribution from the original output. The hallucination distribution is induced by perturbing inputs (visual corruption v′v^{\prime} (Leng et al., 2024), adversarial prompts x′x^{\prime} (Wang et al., 2024c), or attention masking (Huo et al., 2024)). Subsequently, a new contrastive probability distribution is computed by leveraging the differences between these two distributions. This contrastive distribution, denoted as pc​dp_{cd}, is defined as:

pc​d​(y∣v,v′,x′)=softmax\displaystyle p_{cd}\left(y\mid v,v^{\prime},x^{\prime}\right)=\operatorname{softmax} [(1+α)logitθ(y∣v,x)\displaystyle\left[(1+\alpha)\operatorname{logit}_{\theta}\left(y\mid v,x\right)\right. (4)
−αlogitθ(y∣v′,x′)],\displaystyle\left.-\alpha\operatorname{logit}_{\theta}\left(y\mid v^{\prime},x^{\prime}\right)\right],

where larger α\alpha values indicate a stronger amplification of differences between the two distributions (α=0\alpha=0 degenerates to Vanilla decoding). A fundamental limitation of Equation 4 is that the CD subtraction operation can drive certain reasonably token logits to extremely small or negative values, causing unreasonably low-probability tokens to emerge after softmax normalization and thus amplifying tail token probabilities. This necessitates a uniform penalization constraint that suppresses all low-probability outputs from the original inputs:

\displaystyle 𝒱head(y<t)={yt∈𝒱:\displaystyle\mathcal{V}_{\text{head}}\left(y_{<t}\right)=\{y_{t}\in\mathcal{V}: (5)
pθ(yt∣v,x,y<t)≥βmaxwpθ(w∣v,x,y<t)},\displaystyle p_{\theta}\left(y_{t}\mid v,x,y_{<t}\right)\geq\beta\max_{w}p_{\theta}\left(w\mid v,x,y_{<t}\right)\},

where 𝒱\mathcal{V} is the output vocabulary of LVLMs and β\beta is a hyperparameter in [0,1][0,1] for controlling the truncation of the next token distribution. Larger β\beta indicates more aggressive truncation, keeping only high-probability tokens. Combining the CD and the plausibility constraint, we obtain the full formulation:

3.2 Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD)

Existing CD methods (Equation 6) perform contrastive subtraction in the discrete logit space, where even small perturbations can cause abrupt redistributions over the vocabulary, degrading linguistic coherence and necessitating ad-hoc penalty terms (Equation 5). We propose Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD), a lightweight plug-in that introduces contrastive operations into the continuous attention layer, complementing logit-level CD to jointly suppress hallucinations. The complete framework is illustrated in Figure 2.

Motivation.

Attention weights reside in a continuous probability simplex produced by the Softmax operator, where arithmetic combinations yield semantically smooth transitions (Vaswani et al., 2017; Castin et al., 2023). In contrast, logit subtraction operates on unbounded pre-softmax scores whose exponentiation amplifies minor differences into drastic probability shifts. By intervening before the logit stage, ACD modulates where the model attends rather than what it outputs, inherently preserving the linguistic structure of the downstream distribution.

Formulation.

At decoding step tt, we compute attention weights under two input configurations—the original input (v,x)(v,x) and a hallucination-inducing input (v′,x′)(v^{\prime},x^{\prime}):

Atclean\displaystyle A_{t}^{\text{clean}} =Softmax⁡(qt​K≤tclean⊤d),\displaystyle=\mathrm{Softmax}\!\left(\frac{q_{t}\,{K_{\leq t}^{\text{clean}}}^{\!\top}}{\sqrt{d}}\right), (7)
Atnoisy\displaystyle A_{t}^{\text{noisy}} =Softmax⁡(qt​K≤tnoisy⊤d),\displaystyle=\mathrm{Softmax}\!\left(\frac{q_{t}\,{K_{\leq t}^{\text{noisy}}}^{\!\top}}{\sqrt{d}}\right),

where qt∈ℝ1×dq_{t}\!\in\!\mathbb{R}^{1\times d} is the query at step tt, and K≤tclean,K≤tnoisy∈ℝt×dK_{\leq t}^{\text{clean}},\,K_{\leq t}^{\text{noisy}}\!\in\!\mathbb{R}^{t\times d} are cached key matrices under the respective inputs. Unlike logit-level CD (Equation 6), ACD performs contrastive subtraction directly on attention weights:

Atbase=(1+α)​Atclean−α​Atnoisy,A_{t}^{\text{base}}=(1+\alpha)\,A_{t}^{\text{clean}}-\alpha\,A_{t}^{\text{noisy}}, (8)

where α>0\alpha>0 controls the contrastive strength. This operation amplifies attention on regions consistently highlighted by the clean model while suppressing those emphasized only under noise. For generality, we apply ACD uniformly across all decoder layers and attention heads.

Compatibility with Existing CD.

ACD serves as a modular alternative to the logit-level subtraction and penalty mechanism shared by existing CD methods. Given any hallucination induction strategy (e.g., noise injection in VCD, adversarial prompts in ICD, attention masking in SID), ACD performs the contrastive operation at the attention layer instead of the logit layer, thereby inheriting each method’s hallucination-inducing capability while avoiding the coherence degradation and auxiliary penalty terms inherent in logit-level subtraction.

3.3 Adaptive Subtraction Strategy (ASS)

Equation 8 applies uniform subtraction across all positions, implicitly assuming that noise universally inflates attention on irrelevant regions. In practice, however, the effect of noise is bidirectional. We analyze attention shifts between AtcleanA_{t}^{\text{clean}} and AtnoisyA_{t}^{\text{noisy}} over 500 COCO image-caption pairs and observe two distinct phenomena: (i) approximately 32% of positions exhibit attention degradation (Atclean>AtnoisyA_{t}^{\text{clean}}>A_{t}^{\text{noisy}}), where noise obscures valid visual features; (ii) the remaining 68% show attention inflation (Atclean≤AtnoisyA_{t}^{\text{clean}}\leq A_{t}^{\text{noisy}}), indicating hallucination risk. Applying uniform subtraction to group (i) would counter-productively penalize ground-truth regions. Motivated by this finding, we propose the Adaptive Subtraction Strategy (ASS), which applies position-dependent operations:

  • •

    Case 1 — Signal Amplification (Atclean​[i]>Atnoisy​[i]A_{t}^{\text{clean}}[i]>A_{t}^{\text{noisy}}[i]). Noise has degraded attention on semantically valid regions. Rather than subtracting, we amplify these positions to reinforce correct visual grounding.

  • •

    Case 2 — Hallucination Suppression (Atclean​[i]≤Atnoisy​[i]A_{t}^{\text{clean}}[i]\leq A_{t}^{\text{noisy}}[i]). Elevated attention signals attraction to spurious correlations. We apply contrastive suppression to attenuate these high-risk positions.

Formulation.

We define a binary hallucination-risk mask Mt=𝕀⁡(Atnoisy>Atclean)∈{0,1}LM_{t}=\mathbb{I}\!\left(A_{t}^{\text{noisy}}>A_{t}^{\text{clean}}\right)\in\{0,1\}^{L} and compute the modulated attention as:

AtACD=(1+α)​Atclean⏟Global Amplification−α⁡(Atnoisy⊙Mt)⏟Selective Suppression,A_{t}^{\text{ACD}}=\underbrace{(1+\alpha)\,A_{t}^{\text{clean}}\vphantom{\big|}}_{\text{Global Amplification}}\;-\;\underbrace{\alpha\left(A_{t}^{\text{noisy}}\odot M_{t}\right)\vphantom{\big|}}_{\text{Selective Suppression}}, (9)

where ⊙\odot denotes element-wise multiplication. The formulation elegantly unifies both cases: when Mt​[i]=0M_{t}[i]\!=\!0 (Case 1), the subtraction term vanishes and the clean attention is amplified by (+α)(1\!+\!\alpha); when Mt​[i]=1M_{t}[i]\!=\!1 (Case 2), contrastive subtraction actively suppresses spurious activations. As visualized in Figure 3, ASS does not merely restore the clean attention map—it actively expands the margin between relevant and irrelevant regions, functioning as a bidirectional signal-to-noise filter that enhances discriminative power beyond the original clean baseline.

4 Experiments

4.1 Experimental Settings

Following established evaluation protocols from prior work (Leng et al., 2024; Huo et al., 2024; An et al., 2025), we assess our method’s efficacy across standard benchmarks. Comprehensive details regarding datasets, evaluation metrics, case studies, and additional ablation experiments are provided in the Appendix H.

Benchmarks. CHAIR (Yue et al., 2024): Quantifies hallucination using image annotations rather than lexical similarity. Primary metrics include C​H​A​I​RsCHAIR_{s} (sentence-level), C​H​A​I​RiCHAIR_{i} (instance-level), and recall for measuring semantic comprehensiveness. LLaVA-Bench (In-the-Wild) (Liu et al., 2023b): Evaluates generalization through 24 challenging images (memes, paintings, sketches) with 60 questions. Performance assessed by GPT-5 (OpenAI, 2025) on factual accuracy and descriptive richness. POPE (Li et al., 2023c): A binary classification framework (20,000+ QA pairs) assessing object hallucination through yes/no questions with random, popular, and adversarial sampling strategies. Performance measured via Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1. MME (Fu et al., 2023a): Comprehensive evaluation across 14 subtasks spanning perception (object existence, color, position) and cognition (reasoning, computation). Each image features complementary yes/no questions evaluated through accuracy metrics.

Implementation Details. We evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed ACD on several established LVLMs, including LLaVA-1.5 (Liu et al., 2023b) (7B and 13B) with MLP projection layers and Qwen-VL (7B) (Bai et al., 2023) with q-former projection layers. All experiments are conducted on NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs unless otherwise specified. LLaVA-1.5-13B requires an A6000 GPU due to memory constraints. By default, all models refer to 7B variants (e.g., LLaVA-1.5, Qwen-VL) unless explicitly stated. To demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, we compare ACD against established CD strategies designed for hallucination mitigation in LVLMs, including VCD (Leng et al., 2024), ICD (Wang et al., 2024c), and SID (Huo et al., 2024). Furthermore, we integrate ACD into these existing contrastive frameworks to evaluate its compatibility and effectiveness across diverse hallucination-inducing scenarios. Specifically, we denote X+ACD as the variant where the original logit-level subtraction and adaptive penalty terms in method X are entirely replaced with our attention-level subtraction combined with the ASS strategy; no logit-level contrastive subtraction or penalty filtering (Equation 5) is applied. Thus, all X+ACD results reflect ACD operating as a standalone decoding mechanism under different noise constructions. For VCD+ACD, the integration is straightforward as no special handling is required. For ICD+ACD, we ensure identical prompt lengths between original and hallucination-induced inputs to maintain attention alignment. For SID+ACD, we first mask high-weight patches and apply smoothing, then perform attention-layer subtraction. Note that throughout all experiments, we maintain consistent hyperparameters and employ sampling as the default decoding strategy.

4.2 Experimental Results

Experiments on CHAIR. Unlike binary response paradigms (yes/no) in POPE and MME, the CHAIR dataset requires detailed descriptive generation, increasing hallucination susceptibility. Table 1 compares three representative CD baselines (VCD, ICD, SID) across two architectures (LLaVA-1.5, Qwen-VL), revealing three key findings: (1) Consistent hallucination reduction. ACD integration yields substantial improvements across all configurations. For LLaVA-1.5, ACD reduces C​h​a​i​riChair_{i} by 11.7% (VCD: 16.2→\to14.3), 10.3% (ICD: 15.5→\to13.9), and 5.7% (SID: 14.1→\to13.3) while improving recall. Qwen-VL shows comparable gains (VCD+ACD: 8.8% reduction to C​h​a​i​riChair_{i} 12.5), demonstrating that ACD’s generalizability enables seamless integration into CD methods. (2) Simultaneous improvements in accuracy and coverage. ACD simultaneously improves both dimensions across all 6 configurations: recall increases by 0.6-2.3 points alongside hallucination reductions. ACD and ASS smoothly suppress attention to hallucination-prone regions while enhancing grounded object attention, enabling detailed yet accurate captions. (3) Architecture-agnostic gains. Despite architectural differences, improvements remain consistent: LLaVA-1.5 and Qwen-VL achieve 9.2% and 8.4% average C​h​a​i​riChair_{i} reductions with 1.9 and 1.3 point recall gains respectively. This stability indicates ACD exploits fundamental transformer attention properties rather than model-specific artifacts.

Results on LLaVA-Bench-Wild. Following established protocols (Leng et al., 2024; Huo et al., 2024; An et al., 2025), we employ GPT-5 (OpenAI, 2025) as an independent assessor to score Accuracy (factual correctness) and Detail (comprehensiveness) on a 10-point scale. Results are reported in Table 4.1. Integrating ACD with VCD yields consistent gains across both models. On LLaVA-1.5, VCD+ACD improves total Accuracy by +1.80 (4.30→\to6.10) and Detail by +0.65 (4.75→\to5.40). On Qwen-VL, gains are more pronounced: +1.71 Accuracy (5.40→\to7.11) and +0.96 Detail (4.85→\to5.81). Among the three categories, Detail shows the largest boost: +3.00 Accuracy / +1.66 Detail on LLaVA-1.5, and +2.65 / +2.03 on Qwen-VL. This aligns with our motivation—attention-level modulation sharpens focus on fine-grained regions critical for detailed descriptions. Conversational tasks also benefit substantially (+2.16 / +1.86 Accuracy), indicating improved factual grounding in open-ended dialogue. Gains on Complex reasoning are more modest, suggesting such tasks rely more on language priors where logit-level CD remains the primary mechanism.

Results on POPE. Table 5 reports results on the three POPE splits (Random, Popular, Adversarial) when ACD is integrated into VCD, ICD, and SID across LLaVA-1.5 and Qwen-VL. ACD yields consistent F1 improvements across all six baseline–model combinations. On Qwen-VL, VCD+ACD improves F1 by +1.0 on Random (86.8→\to87.8), +0.4 on Popular, and +1.0 on Adversarial. On LLaVA-1.5, the same pairing yields +0.5/+1.2/+1.1 across the three splits. ICD+ACD and SID+ACD exhibit similar trends, confirming ACD’s role as a model- and method-agnostic plug-in. Two observations merit attention. First, the largest gains concentrate on the harder Popular and Adversarial splits, where hallucination pressure is greatest—precisely the regime where adaptive attention modulation (Section 3.3) is most effective. Second, ACD tends to improve Recall more than Precision (e.g., +1.2 Recall vs. −-0.4 Precision for VCD on LLaVA-1.5 Random), suggesting that attention-level reinforcement (Case 1) recovers missed objects without introducing new false positives.

Results on MME. We further evaluate ACD on the MME benchmark using LLaVA-1.5. MME covers 14 subtasks spanning perception (e.g., color, spatial position) and cognition (e.g., reasoning, computation) with a binary yes/no protocol, providing a broad testbed for both hallucination suppression and general capability retention. Results are reported in Table 4.1. ACD consistently improves both Perception and Cognition scores across all three baselines. VCD+ACD raises Perception by +22.3 (1475.4→\to1497.7) and Cognition by +14.2 (284.3→\to298.5). ICD+ACD and SID+ACD follow the same trend, with SID+ACD achieving the highest overall scores (1518.7 / 299.1). Notably, the Cognition gains indicate that attention-level modulation does not sacrifice higher-order reasoning for perceptual fidelity—a common trade-off in logit-level CD methods. This confirms that ACD serves as a general-purpose plug-in that enhances factual grounding while preserving model versatility.

Generalization to Modern Architectures. To validate ACD on recent LVLMs, we evaluate on Qwen3-VL (Bai et al., 2025) (2025) at both 4B and 8B scales. Table 4 reports CHAIR hallucination metrics alongside generation quality scores on the same benchmark. ACD consistently reduces hallucination while fully recovering the coherence that logit-level VCD degrades. On Qwen3-VL-4B, ACD lowers Chairi\text{Chair}_{i} by 22.8% (11.4→\to8.8) while improving Recall by 2.6 points; coherence metrics (CIDEr, BLEU-4, GPT-5) return to baseline levels. On Qwen3-VL-8B, we observe that VCD produces 12.8% malformed outputs on POPE and 69.2% on MME (e.g., infinite non-English token loops), a catastrophic failure caused by logit subtraction suppressing EOS probability below the penalty threshold in deeper architectures. ACD exhibits zero malformed outputs, as attention-level intervention preserves the natural token ranking without penalty mechanisms. These results confirm that ACD generalizes to modern architectures and that the coherence degradation problem of logit-level CD becomes more severe as models scale deeper.

4.3 Ablation Study and Analysis

Ablation on Components. Table 6 isolates the contribution of each component in our framework. We compare five configurations: Regular decoding, VCD without/with its penalty term, and ACD without/with ASS. Rows 2–3 show that VCD’s penalty mechanism reduces hallucination (Chairs: 53.4→\to51.8) but introduces a threshold hyperparameter. Row 4 replaces the penalty with ACDbase{}_{\text{base}}—uniform attention subtraction (Eq. 8) without ASS—and achieves comparable Chairs (52.1) while being threshold-free, confirming that attention-level intervention is inherently smooth. Adding ASS (row 5) brings further gains: Chairs drops by 1.1 (52.1→\to51.0), Chairi by 1.3 (15.6→\to14.3), and Recall rises by 0.9 (77.4→\to78.3). These improvements stem from ASS’s ability to reinforce informative tokens (Case 1) while selectively suppressing hallucination triggers (Case 2), as visualized in Figure 3. The full VCD+ACD framework achieves the best trade-off, reducing Chairs by 3.1 and improving Recall by 4.9 over Regular decoding.

Causal Validation of ASS. To directly validate that ASS’s two cases correspond to their intended semantic roles, we conduct an attention-object alignment analysis on 500 COCO images. We extract AtcleanA_{t}^{\text{clean}} and AtnoisyA_{t}^{\text{noisy}} over visual tokens and measure each group’s attention mass within ground-truth bounding boxes versus hallucinated regions identified by the CHAIR pipeline. Case 1 positions (Aclean>AnoisyA^{\text{clean}}>A^{\text{noisy}}) allocate 74.2% of attention to ground-truth objects and only 12.5% to hallucinated regions, while Case 2 positions show the opposite pattern (18.7% vs. 61.3%). This confirms that ASS’s binary mask correctly distinguishes signal degradation from hallucination risk without requiring any tunable threshold.

Efficiency. Since ACD replaces logit-level subtraction rather than adding to it, it bypasses the vocabulary projection and penalty sorting for the noisy branch. On POPE (LLaVA-1.5, RTX 3090), VCD+ACD is 8.2% faster (0.493s vs. 0.537s per example) and uses 3.2% less GPU memory (15.3G vs. 15.8G) compared to standard VCD (detailed in Appendix I).

Coherence Analysis. CHAIR requires detailed descriptive generation rather than binary yes/no responses, making it well-suited for evaluating output coherence. Table 7 compares generation quality across Regular, VCD, and VCD+ACD decoding. VCD degrades coherence substantially: CIDEr drops by 13.2% (0.266→\to0.231), BLEU-4 by 42.6% (0.094→\to0.054), and GPT-5-assisted scores by 6.5% (0.920→\to0.860). This stems from logit-level subtraction disrupting vocabulary distributions and penalty terms (Eq. 5) forcing suboptimal token choices. VCD+ACD fully recovers—and slightly exceeds—baseline coherence: CIDEr returns to 0.266, BLEU-4 rises to 0.096 (+2.1% over Regular), and GPT-5 scores reach 0.980 (+6.5%). Two factors drive these gains: (1) attention-level intervention preserves linguistic structure by avoiding abrupt vocabulary shifts; (2) ASS selectively suppresses hallucination-prone regions while amplifying semantic content, yielding more faithful generation. Combined with the hallucination reductions in Table 1 (Chairs: −-3.1, Chairi: −-4.2), these results confirm that ACD resolves the quality–hallucination trade-off inherent in logit-level contrastive decoding.

5 Conclusion

This paper tackles the challenge of balancing hallucination suppression with output coherence in LVLMs. We show that existing CD methods degrade generation quality due to logit-level operations and restrictive penalty mechanisms. To address this, we propose ACD, a plug-and-play framework that shifts contrastive operations to the attention layer. The inherent smoothness of attention-level intervention preserves linguistic structure, while ASS dynamically suppresses hallucination-prone attention patterns and reinforces semantic content. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ACD consistently reduces hallucinations across multiple benchmarks without sacrificing—and often improving—coherence metrics. By targeting hallucinations at their attentional source rather than through post-hoc logit adjustment, ACD offers a principled solution that enhances LVLM reliability for real-world deployment.

Impact Statement

This paper presents work whose goal is to advance the field of Machine Learning. There are many potential societal consequences of our work, none which we feel must be specifically highlighted here.
